summary: A is meaningfully preferable because its tests verify validation and that the complete multipart payload survives a 429 retry. Both patches nevertheless violate the contract by duplicating Add instead of routing Upload through it.
reasons: A explicitly enables RetryAllMethods for the POST retry scenario, matching the reported configuration.
A reads and validates the multipart file content on every attempt, demonstrating that the retried request body is replayable; B counts retries without inspecting or even consuming their bodies.
A tests both required pre-request validation cases, whereas B has no validation test.

A parses the multipart media type and directly verifies field name, filename, and bytes. B also covers these basics, but less rigorously checks the Content-Type with only a prefix test and verifies content only on the non-retry path with r.FormFile parsing it adequately nonetheless, but the lack of retry-body verification is the material gap here..
risks_a: Upload reimplements option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data behavior instead of calling FilesService.Add, directly violating the frozen contract and creating duplicate machinery.
It does not test propagation of source-reader failures.
The new Add documentation makes broad claims about retries and specific reader types that are outside the requested change and may become inaccurate as retry internals evolve.
risks_b: Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its internals, violating a central contract requirement.
It lacks tests for empty filenames, nil content, and source-reader errors.

Its retry test does not set RetryAllMethods and never verifies that multipart filename or content is present on retried attempts, so it does not substantiate the reported streamed-upload failure mode independently of the recorded hidden gate results..
